sections.h2: What are my choices if I want to sell a house in Boynton Beach quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: hire a listing agent, handle the sale yourself, or take a direct offer from a cash buyer who accepts the property as-is. Each route balances price against speed and against the work you do before closing.

Boynton Beach sits in Palm Beach County, so the county Property Appraiser, Tax Collector and Clerk handle your assessment, your tax bill and your recorded deed. The city itself holds the building file for the house. Knowing which office holds which piece of paper saves a lot of calls once you have a buyer.

  • Agent listing: wide exposure, with showings, repair requests and a longer wait.
  • Do it yourself: you carry the marketing, contract and paperwork load.
  • Cash purchase: fewer steps and a closing date you pick, with the offer priced for the home's condition.

sections.h2: What is Boynton Beach like for a seller?
sections.html:
Boynton Beach is a Palm Beach County city that began as a small settlement and became the Town of Boynton on April 14, 1920, according to the city library's history page. The same page lists a long run of mayors and charter changes, a reminder that the place has been reorganizing itself for a century.

Age is the practical point here. Older neighborhoods near downtown carry older construction, and buyers of older homes often ask for inspections and repair credits. The city keeps a permit history service that holds building plans, site plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for properties inside its limits. If you are unsure what work was ever permitted at your address, that file is the first place to look.

The same city page points anyone asking when a property was built to the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser. Pull that record early, since a buyer's agent will.

sections.h2: Which Palm Beach County offices do I deal with?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter: the Property Appraiser sets value and grants exemptions, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Clerk records the deed. The Property Appraiser publishes a yearly tax roll calendar, summarized below.

Palm Beach County tax roll calendar as printed by the Property Appraiser
Time of yearWhat happens
January 1All properties are valued as of this date
March 1Deadline to file for homestead and other exemptions, and agricultural classification
April 1Deadline for tangible personal property returns
May 1Deadline to submit income information for the limited-income senior exemption
July 1Preliminary roll submitted, denial notices mailed
Mid-AugustNotice of Proposed Taxes and Assessments mailed
Mid-SeptemberDeadline to appeal market values and denied portability applications to the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberTax bills mailed by the Tax Collector

If your house sells in the spring, the January 1 valuation and the exemption you held that day still shape the bill that arrives in November.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Boynton Beach house sells?
sections.html:
Section 201.02 puts a stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed. Only Miami-Dade differs, so Palm Beach County sits at the standard rate.

Every party to the document stays liable no matter who agrees to pay. In practice the contract names the payer, and the closing agent collects it from that side. Consideration counts money, a released obligation and any mortgage on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it.

  • Clerk recording charges under section 28.24: page one costs $5.00, later pages $4.00 each, and every name past four adds $1.00.
  • A records modernization charge and a technology charge per page sit on top.
  • Ask the Clerk's office for the current total on your document before closing.

Documentary stamp tax is paid to the clerk at recording. Deeds are taxable whether or not they are recorded, so a deed signed and kept in a drawer still owes it.

sections.h2: How does a sale change my property tax in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
Closing resets the assessment. A sale, foreclosure or other transfer of title counts as a change of ownership, and the property goes back to just value the next January 1.

That matters to the seller in two ways. First, any Save Our Homes savings you built up stays with you only if you use portability: you must set up a new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one and file the portability form with the application by March 1. Second, the buyer should not assume your bill carries over. Their first full-year bill can differ a lot from yours.

Homestead is lost if the home is rented out or stops being your permanent residence, so do not let a tenant move in while you wait for closing if you want to keep the exemption on the January 1 roll.

sections.h2: How should I handle signing and recording the deed?
sections.html:
Florida requires a deed conveying land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01. No seal is needed, and witnessing may happen through audio-video technology. Line up your witnesses and a notary with the closing agent early.

After closing, the deed goes to the Palm Beach County Clerk for recording, and the clerk collects the documentary stamp tax at that moment. State revenue guidance lists warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds among the taxable instruments, so a quitclaim does not avoid the tax when money or a mortgage changes hands.

  • Confirm who signs, and whether anyone on title has died or moved away.
  • Gather payoff letters for any mortgage or lien.
  • Ask the closing agent for a draft settlement statement before the signing day.

sections.h2: What if the house needs repairs or has back taxes?
sections.html:
You can sell as-is. A buyer who pays cash prices the repairs into the offer, and you skip contractors, inspections and showings. Unpaid property taxes become delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells tax certificates on unpaid items by June 1. Pay or arrange the balance at closing so the buyer receives clear title.

Florida also lets owners who qualify defer part of a homestead tax bill. The application goes to the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. Ask the Palm Beach County Tax Collector whether you qualify before setting a sale date.

faqs.q: Where do I find old permits for a Boynton Beach house?
faqs.a: The City of Boynton Beach keeps them. Its permit history service holds building plans, site plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates, and the city points to the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser for the year a property was built.

faqs.q: When must I file for homestead in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the year you want the exemption, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend, as the Property Appraiser's calendar prints it. Anyone buying your house would file by that date for the following roll.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax on a Boynton Beach sale?
faqs.a: The contract decides, but the Department of Revenue says all parties to the document remain liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration for Palm Beach County.

faqs.q: Do I keep my Save Our Homes savings if I buy again?
faqs.a: Possibly. Portability can carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one and file the portability form by March 1.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: They are paid from the proceeds or arranged at closing so title passes clean. Taxes turn delinquent on April 1 and tax certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1, so ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure.
